key_insight: High-throughput first-principles calculations show that delafossite oxides can compete in stability with infinite-layer AB O2 phases, especially for Ni, Pd, and Pt systems, while favoring different electronic structure and cation order.
engineering_relevance: The results guide materials selection and doping strategies for synthesizing stable layered oxides and optimizing candidates for next-generation correlated-electron and superconducting devices.
method: Comprehensive high-throughput DFT screening across AB O2 oxides
Phase-diagram comparison of infinite-layer, delafossite, and ordered rock-salt (111) variants
Electronic-structure analysis of Fermi-surface character and cation ordering
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a broad first-principles survey showing delafossites rival infinite-layer phases in thermodynamic stability and that La-Ni is the thermodynamic optimum, with Ca/Sr/Ba hole doping systematically improving infinite-layer stability.
watch_item: Thermodynamic favorability from DFT does not guarantee successful synthesis or device performance, especially for substrate-free bulk phases and kinetic constraints.
paper_title: Delafossites as an unexpected competing phase to infinite-layer oxides
